summary: Submitted the VerifyLeader probe for retained execution against the question I registered last turn. The setup uses a real four-voter cluster and demotes one voter to nonvoter through the exported DemoteVoter contract, so the configuration is three voters plus one nonvoter; the interrupted trial partitions the leader together with the nonvoter and the control partitions the leader alone. Rather than assuming reachability from stale contact timestamps, the events separate the partition side (which suffrages the harness left with the leader) from the observed outcome — the exported verification result, the vote tally the future ended with, and the quorum size it was measured against — and a third event records whether the voters the leader cannot reach elected their own leader and committed an entry, with the indexes that make that checkable. Two comparisons declare the discriminating pair (nonvoter-only side confirms leadership; no-peer side does not) and a third declares that the confirmation coexists with a newer commit the interrupted leader never applied, which is what makes the confirmation unsound as a basis for a consistent read. Native feedback from the local dry run, explicitly not retained evidence: with only the nonvoter on the leader's side the verification succeeded with votes 2 against quorum 2 while the same leader with no peer returned ErrLeadershipLost with votes 1, and in the first case the two detached voters elected a leader that committed index 6 while the interrupted leader stayed at applied index 4. The harness compiles and runs cleanly, and I corrected one mislabeled operand before submitting so nothing reports pre-partition contact as reachability.
